_comment: No-tracker profile. The pipeline still runs end-to-end: issues become markdown files under <PATHS_SPECS_DIR>/../issues/, the lock is a directory (mkdir is atomic on POSIX), and PR-linking keywords render as plain prose. Use this to trial the workflow before wiring a real tracker, or in repos where work is tracked out-of-band.

tracker.TRACKER_LOCK_MECHANISM: a lock DIRECTORY under .ai/issues/.locks/ — `mkdir` fails if it already exists, which is the atomic compare-and-set POSIX gives us for free (a lock FILE via `touch` is not atomic and must not be substituted)

notes: The lock is a directory, not a file, because `mkdir` is the only POSIX filesystem primitive that atomically fails-if-exists without a race. A lockfile created with `touch` or `[ -f ] && touch` has a check-then-act window two agents can both pass through.
This profile is single-machine only. A shared network filesystem does not reliably give mkdir atomicity across hosts — use a real tracker for a distributed fleet.
TRACKER_SET_STATUS is empty: `ct render` drops board-status prose entirely when the tracker has no board, rather than rendering instructions for a mechanism that does not exist.
